column11: Baxfendy (baxdrostat, AstraZeneca) WAC of $900 per 30 tablets, once daily: $30 a day x 365 = $10,950 a year. $10,950 is the annual WAC ICER's August 2026 hypertension draft evidence report used for baxdrostat, with an identical placeholder for lorundrostat (AJMC, 'ICER Draft Flags High Cost of New Hypertension Drug Class', ajmc.com/view/icer-draft-flags-high-cost-of-new-hypertension-drug-class). Fierce Pharma ('AZ's blood pressure newcomer Baxfendy fails to meet cost-effectiveness bar, ICER says') reports the same $900 per 30 tablets annualised as twelve fills, $10,800
column12: Judgement on the comparator. The brief says a published annual list price beats the CMS convention, and Baxfendy is the closest marketed product in the same disease and setting. Its label (DailyMed, in the book's labels table, effective 2026-09-18) covers hypertension in adults not adequately controlled on other agents, and the book's Hypertension pool was drawn for it. It has no CMS demand row yet. Cross-check: Leqvio, the same-modality twice-yearly siRNA, reads $6,135 per CMS Part B beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Leqvio: $296,288,761 over 48,298). Less the 6% Part B add-on, that is a net $5,788, close to the $5,184 net here. Case for higher: if ZENITH succeeds, zilebesiran carries an outcomes claim that Baxfendy's label says it lacks ('There are no controlled trials demonstrating risk reduction'). Case for lower: ICER found the aldosterone synthase inhibitors far above its value benchmarks at this price, which signals payer resistance to branded antihypertensives against generics. Discrepancy to flag: the book's baxdrostat seed prices Baxfendy off Leqvio's Part D $5,364, but Leqvio's Medicare beneficiaries sit 95% in Part B, and Baxfendy now has its own WAC

column11: Measured on Entresto, the book's closest cardiovascular oral brand with a CMS negotiated price. CMS Part D 2024 gross: $4,020,321,686 over 364,166,283 tablets = $11.0398 a tablet (lookup.py demand Entresto). The Maximum Fair Price for 2026 is $5.2266 a tablet, NDC 00078-0659 (book negotiated_prices, cms_mfp; $295 per 30-day equivalent supply). 1 - 5.2266 / 11.0398 = 0.5266
column12: Judgement. A WAC anchor takes neither house convention, so the discount is sourced. Direction checked: 0.527 comes off list, and net is $5,184 a patient-year. Case for a smaller discount: a Maximum Fair Price is negotiated for a drug seven or more years past launch, so it sits below what a new launch realises (backend/gross_to_net.py says so). If zilebesiran is buy-and-bill under Part B, as Leqvio is, only the 6% add-on comes off an ASP that is already net. Case for a larger one: the gross figure is 2024 and the MFP is 2026, so list-price growth in between understates the discount slightly, and primary-care hypertension is a heavily rebated generic-dominated class. The house 0.5 on a CMS Part D figure would give almost the same net

Pooled 12-month discontinuation is 12.1% (95% CI 7.4-19.0) across alirocumab, evolocumab and inclisiran; 12-month persistence is 81.8%
column12: Judgement on the analogue: an injectable CV-prevention agent added to cheap orals, closest to zilebesiran's infrequent dosing. It is the same value the book's olpasiran and lepodisiran seeds carry. Those seeds call it an inclisiran figure, but the pooled studies are mostly alirocumab and evolocumab, and the paper notes limited inclisiran evidence. Case for higher: 1 minus the 81.8% persistence gives 0.182, and the paper finds persistence declining beyond 12 months. Hypertension is asymptomatic, and oral antihypertensive persistence is worse. Case for lower: an HCP-administered injection twice a year needs two visits a year. Discrepancy to flag: the baxdrostat seed's discontinuation source is text about advanced solid tumours

column12: Judgement on the timeline. Topline around late 2030, an NDA in 2031 and a standard review put launch around late 2031 or early 2032, so 2032 is the first full year. This is the same two-calendar-years-after-PCD rule the verified vepugratinib (PCD 2029-10 to 2031) and duvakitug (2028-09 to 2030) seeds use. Case for later: ZENITH is event-driven, so the PCD can slip with the event rate. Alnylam states a launch year for nucresiran ('by 2030', 10-Q 0001178670-26-000062) but none for zilebesiran. The margin is 1 - 0.182331 - 0.325992 - 0.355357 = 0.13632, with other_costs_pct at nil, as the house charge rebuild on the company rows this seed now carries leaves it. 'Low double digit' is taken at its 10% floor, as the votoplam seed does, so ex-US is 0.10 / 0.13632 = 0.7336. (0.5 + 1.0835 x 0.7336) / 2.0835 = 0.6215. Recompute if the charge moves: at a 0.20 margin the share is 0.500, and at the ~30% non-GAAP operating margin Alnylam targets through 2030 (FY2025 10-K MD&A) it is 0.413. At a 12% royalty it is 0.698, and at 15% (ex-US capped at 1.0) 0.760. Not in this field: up to $2.15bn of further Roche milestones receivable; $243mm Alnylam owes Blackstone in 16 quarterly payments on approval, a fixed payment not a royalty (10-Q note 9); and the 40/60 development cost split against a 50/50 US profit split

column11: Three NHANES papers. (1) Uncontrolled at 140/90, ZENITH's floor: of US adults on antihypertensives, 5.7% take three classes and 2.8% four or more with BP at or above 140/90, against 19.7% with aTRH by the 2018 AHA definition. 8.5 / 19.7 = 0.431472 of the resistant pool (Carey RM et al., Hypertension 2019;73:424-431, doi:10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.118.12191, PMID 30580690). (2) Two-drug patients, whom ZENITH enrols and the resistant pool excludes: of treated US adults with BP at or above 140/90 in 2013-2016, 40.2% take one class and 35.1% two, so 24.7% take three or more; two-drug patients are 35.1 / 24.7 = 1.421053 times the three-plus group (Derington CG et al., Hypertension 2020;75:973-981, doi:10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.119.14360, PMID 32148129). (3) Established CVD (prior MI, HF or stroke): 36.4% of uncontrolled aTRH, and 15.9% of adults controlled on fewer than three drugs (Kaczmarski KR et al., BMC Nephrol 2019;20:138, doi:10.1186/s12882-019-1315-0, PMID 31023262). 0.431472 x 0.364 = 0.157056 on three or more drugs; 0.431472 x 1.421053 x 0.159 = 0.097490 on two; total 0.254546
column12: Judgement: a sourced floor for ZENITH's label, uncontrolled hypertension on two or more antihypertensives (one a diuretic) with established CVD or high CV risk. The book's pool is the resistant population, so eligible_pct carries the two-drug patients the trial enrols (0.613 of the pool before the CVD filter) and the CVD filter the pool lacks. Applied to the book's pool: 3.73mm US patients. Floor on two counts: the two-drug group takes the 15.9% CVD share Kaczmarski measured in adults controlled on one or two drugs, where uncontrolled two-drug patients likely carry more; and the trial's high-CV-risk arm without established CVD is not counted, because no US share for it was found. Ceiling if every uncontrolled patient on two or more drugs qualified: 0.431 + 0.613 = 1.045. Kaczmarski's CVD definition leaves out angina, revascularisation and PAD. Case for lower: ZENITH requires a diuretic (86.8% of aTRH take one, Kaczmarski; the share among two-drug patients is not given, though ACE inhibitor or ARB plus diuretic is the commonest dual regimen, Derington), excludes five or more drugs (8.49% of aTRH, Earle WB et al., Hypertension 2026, PMID 41778325), and NHANES single-visit BP counts white-coat and non-adherent patients. Derington groups diuretics as one class and Carey does not, so the 1.42 ratio is taken within Derington; Derington's own three-plus share (31.0% x 24.7% = 7.7% of treated) sits near Carey's 8.5%

column11: Solved in the engine (forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock, with the ramp and discontinuation here) to reproduce Leqvio's measured capture at the same age. Leqvio had 50,979 Medicare beneficiaries in 2024, its third full year after approval in December 2021: Part B 48,298 plus Part D 2,681 (lookup.py demand Leqvio). Its pool is the 18.7mm US adults with ASCVD, of whom 61.4% are recommended add-on lipid-lowering therapy = 11.48mm (Alanaeme CJ et al., Am Heart J Plus 2022;21:100201, doi:10.1016/j.ahjo.2022.100201, PMID 37168932). Share 0.444%. The engine reaches it at year index 2 with a peak of 0.01768
column12: Judgement: the multiple is 1.0, so zilebesiran takes its eligible pool at the pace Leqvio took its own. Cross-check: Leqvio's all-payer US revenue of $575mm in 2025 (index 3), at the Part B net of $5,788 a beneficiary, is about 99,300 patient-years, or 0.865% of the pool. The engine needs 0.01727 to match that, so the two measures agree. The Medicare count can double-count patients in both Parts, and it leaves out non-Medicare patients. Case for higher: zilebesiran would launch with outcomes data, which Leqvio lacked (ORION-4 pending), with twice-yearly dosing aimed at hypertension non-adherence, and with Roche's scale. Case for lower: oral aldosterone synthase inhibitors (Baxfendy launched 2026; lorundrostat) arrive years earlier and cheaper. Hypertension is run in primary care, where in-office injectables are less established than in lipid clinics. ICER's finding on the ASIs signals payer friction. On this peak and the corrected eligible share (0.254546, 3.73mm US), the US treated stock reaches about 0.29mm by year 9 and 0.62mm by year 14 at the engine's default carryover (engine run). Held stationary (carryover 0.924242) the peak re-solves to 0.019624 and the stock is 0.22mm and 0.39mm. Re-solved to 0.019624 on the same Leqvio target (0.44% of the pool on therapy in its third full year) once the stationary carryover is set, per the second reader's engine run; it was 0.017679 on an unbounded pool
